stem: What is the main job of a network interface card (NIC)?

options.content: It connects a computer to the network medium
options.rationale: Correct: it sends and receives the signals.

options.content: It stores the files shared on the network
options.rationale: File storage is the job of a server.

options.content: It joins two different networks together
options.rationale: That is the job of a router.

options.content: It strengthens a signal that has become weak
options.rationale: That is the job of a repeater.

explanation: A NIC connects a device to the network and holds its MAC address.

stem: What does a repeater do?

options.content: It regenerates a weakened signal so that it can travel further
options.rationale: Correct: it overcomes attenuation.

options.content: It joins a LAN to the internet using IP addresses
options.rationale: That is a router.

options.content: It forwards a frame only to the port of its destination
options.rationale: That is a switch.

options.content: It converts a digital signal into radio waves for a laptop or phone
options.rationale: That is a wireless NIC or access point.

explanation: A repeater receives a weak signal and sends out a fresh copy.

stem: What is the purpose of a wireless access point in a school LAN?

options.content: To give each device a MAC address
options.rationale: The MAC address is set in the NIC.

options.content: To store the user accounts
options.rationale: That is the server.

options.content: To connect wireless devices to the wired network
options.rationale: Correct: it links radio to cable.

options.content: To translate private addresses into a public address
options.rationale: That is NAT, done by a router.

explanation: A WAP is the point where radio devices reach the wired LAN.

stem: What is a default gateway?

options.content: The first computer to start up on a LAN
options.rationale: A gateway is a router address, not a computer start order.

options.content: The MAC address of the switch
options.rationale: The gateway is an IP address of a router.

options.content: The cable that joins the switch to the file server in the computer lab
options.rationale: It is an address, not a cable.

options.content: The router address to which a device sends packets for other networks
options.rationale: Correct.

explanation: Packets for addresses outside the LAN go to the default gateway.

stem: Why does a switch usually give better performance than a hub?

options.content: It increases the speed of every cable
options.rationale: A switch does not change the speed of the cables.

options.content: It removes the need for a MAC address
options.rationale: Switches use MAC addresses to forward frames.

options.content: It sends each frame only to the port of the destination
options.rationale: Correct: other devices are not disturbed.

options.content: It broadcasts every frame to every port, whether or not it is needed
options.rationale: That is what a hub does.

explanation: A hub repeats every frame to all ports, so devices share the capacity; a switch forwards selectively.
hints: Compare where the frame is sent in each device.

stem: In CSMA/CD, what happens straight after a device detects a collision?

options.content: It resends the frame at once
options.rationale: Resending immediately would cause another collision.

options.content: It sends the frame to the default gateway of the network
options.rationale: The gateway is not involved in a collision on the LAN.

options.content: It switches to a wireless connection
options.rationale: CSMA/CD does not change the medium.

options.content: It sends a jam signal and stops transmitting
options.rationale: Correct: then it waits a random time.

explanation: After a collision: jam, stop, random back-off, listen, retry.
hints: Recall the five steps in order.

stem: A technician replaces a hub with a switch and finds that collisions almost disappear. Which statement best explains this?

options.content: The switch increases the random back-off time that devices must wait after a collision
options.rationale: The back-off is set by the Ethernet method, not by the switch.

options.content: The switch encrypts all frames
options.rationale: Encryption does not prevent collisions.

options.content: The switch gives each computer a new MAC address
options.rationale: MAC addresses do not change.

options.content: Each device has its own link to a switch port, so frames are not sharing a cable
options.rationale: Correct: no shared medium means no collisions on the link.

explanation: A switched, full-duplex link is not shared, so two devices cannot collide on it.
hints: What was shared when a hub was used?

stem: A router connects different networks and forwards packets using IP addresses.
explanation: True. A router reads the destination IP address and uses its routing table.

stem: A switch sends every frame to every port in the same way as a hub.
explanation: False. A switch forwards a frame to the destination port only, once it has learnt where the destination is.

stem: The MAC address of a device changes when it is moved to a different network.
explanation: False. The MAC address is fixed in the network card. The IP address is the one that changes.
hints: Which address is fixed in the card?

stem: Match each device to its purpose.

right.content: Joins two LAN segments and passes only the frames that need to cross
Lets wireless devices join the wired LAN
Forwards frames to the destination port using MAC addresses
Joins different networks and forwards packets using IP addresses

explanation: Each device works at a different level of the network.

stem: Put the steps of CSMA/CD in order by completing the sentences.

payload.template: A device first {{blank:a}} to the medium. If it is idle the device {{blank:b}}. If it detects a collision it sends a {{blank:c}} signal and then waits a {{blank:d}} time before trying again.

explanation: Listen, transmit, detect, jam, random wait.

stem:
A five-port switch has Rudo on port 1, Farai on port 2, Chipo on port 3, Sipho on port 4 and a printer on port 5. Its address table starts empty. Frames arrive in this order:

1. Farai sends to Printer
2. Printer sends to Farai
3. Rudo sends to Farai
4. Sipho sends to Rudo
5. Farai sends to Sipho

Choose the action the switch takes for frames 1 to 3.
explanation: Frame 1: the printer is unknown, so the frame is flooded. Frame 2: Farai was learnt on port 2, so the reply goes to port 2 only. Frame 3: Farai is known on port 2, so forwarded to port 2.
hints: Learn the sender's port first, then check the destination.

stem: A 24-port switch has an empty address table. A frame arrives on port 6 for a device it has not learnt. To how many ports is the frame sent?
explanation: Flooded to 23 ports.
workedSolution:
1. The destination is unknown, so the frame is flooded.
2. It is sent to every port except port 6.
3. 24 − 1 = 23.
hints: Flooding goes to every port except the one the frame arrived on.

stem:
After frames 1 to 5 below have arrived at the switch (table initially empty), how many devices are in its address table?

1. Farai sends to Printer
2. Printer sends to Farai
3. Rudo sends to Farai
4. Sipho sends to Rudo
5. Farai sends to Sipho
explanation: Senders: Farai, Printer, Rudo and Sipho = 4 devices.
workedSolution:
1. The table learns the sender of each frame: Farai, Printer, Rudo, Sipho.
2. Farai appears twice but is stored once.
3. There are 4 entries.
hints: Count the entries after the frames have been learnt.

stem: Describe how Ethernet uses CSMA/CD when two devices send at the same time. [4]

points.description: Each device listens to check that the medium is idle before it transmits
Both transmit and the signals collide; the devices detect the collision
Each sends a jam signal and stops transmitting
Each waits a random time before listening and trying again

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Each device listens until the medium is idle and then transmits. If two transmit together there is a collision, which both detect. They each send a jam signal and stop, wait a random time and try again.

explanation: Listen, transmit, detect, jam, random wait.

stem: A laptop on a school LAN sends a request to a web server on the internet. Explain the role of the default gateway. [3]

points.description: The destination is outside the laptop's own network
So the laptop sends the packet to the default gateway, which is the address of the router
The router forwards the packet towards the destination network

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The web server is outside the LAN, so the laptop sends the packet to its default gateway, which is the router. The router forwards it towards the destination network.

explanation: Outside address, to the gateway, forwarded by the router.
hints: What does the router do with an outside address?

stem: Explain how a switch decides where to send a frame. [3]

points.description: It reads the destination MAC address in the frame
It looks the address up in its table of MAC addresses and ports
It forwards to that port only, or floods to all other ports if the address is not in the table

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The switch reads the destination MAC address and looks it up in its table. If it is there, the frame goes to that port only. If not, it is sent to all other ports.

explanation: Read, look up, forward or flood.
hints: Mention the table of MAC addresses.

stem: Outline what network address translation (NAT) does. [2]

points.description: The router replaces the private source address of an outgoing packet with its public address
This allows many devices to share one public address / the replies are sent back to the right device

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The router replaces the private source address with its own public address, so many devices can share one public address and replies reach the right device.

explanation: Private to public and sharing.
hints: One mark for what the router replaces, one for the benefit.

stem:
A four-port switch connects Nyasha's PC (port 1), Thandeka's PC (port 2), a file server (port 3) and a printer (port 4). The address table is empty. Frames arrive in this order:

1. Nyasha's PC sends to the server
2. The server sends to Nyasha's PC
3. Thandeka's PC sends to the printer
4. The printer sends to Thandeka's PC

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: What does the switch do with frame 1?

options.content: Sends it to port 3 only
options.rationale: The server's port has not been learnt.

options.content: Floods it to ports 2, 3 and 4
options.rationale: Correct: the server is not in the table yet.

options.content: Discards it
options.rationale: Frames to unknown destinations are flooded, not discarded.

options.content: Sends it to port 1
options.rationale: Port 1 is where it came from.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: What does the switch do with frame 2?

options.content: Floods it to ports 1, 2 and 4
options.rationale: Nyasha's port is known.

options.content: Forwards it to port 1 only
options.rationale: Correct: Nyasha was learnt on port 1.

options.content: Sends it to port 3
options.rationale: Port 3 is where it came from.

options.content: Discards it
options.rationale: It is for another port.

parts.explanation: The destination is in the table.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: To how many ports is frame 3 sent?
parts.workedSolution:
1. The printer has not yet been learnt, so frame 3 is flooded.
2. It is sent to all ports except port 2: ports 1, 3 and 4.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Explain why frame 4 is sent to port 2 only.

points.description: The switch learnt Thandeka's address on port 2 when frame 3 arrived
The destination is in the table, so the frame is forwarded to that port only

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The switch learnt that Thandeka's PC is on port 2 from frame 3, so it forwards the frame to that port only.

explanation: Run the table from empty; the switch learns the sender each time.
hints: Update the table for each frame before choosing the action.
Flood when the destination is not in the table.

stem: A guest lodge near Victoria Falls has 20 rooms in a long single-storey building. The reception computer and a server are connected by cable to a switch. Guests use their own laptops and phones. The lodge also has a link to an internet service provider.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Name the device that lets the guests' laptops join the wired network and state what it does.

points.description: Wireless access point
It sends and receives radio signals and passes data to the wired network

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: A wireless access point. It sends and receives radio signals and connects the guests' devices to the wired network.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Name the device that connects the lodge LAN to the internet and state one thing it does with a packet.

points.description: Router
It reads the destination IP address and forwards the packet towards the internet / replaces the private address (NAT)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: A router. It reads the destination IP address and forwards the packet towards the internet.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: The cable to the last room is longer than the limit and the signal is weak. State the device that can be added and what it does.

points.description: A repeater
It regenerates the weak signal so it can travel further

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: A repeater regenerates the weak signal so it can travel further.

explanation: Switch inside the LAN, router to the internet, wireless access point for laptops, repeater to extend the cable.
hints: Think about which device does each job.
